text:
ashley: Heads up — after yesterday's node image roll (kernel 6.5 + nvidia 560.45) we're seeing ~4% of new GPU nodes in us-central-1 hang during provisioning with DKMS failures.
kevin: saw same in canary, logs show DKMS build failing at link stage, something about rpath to /usr/local/cuda/lib64 not found.
raj: do you have a sample log?
ashley: here —
```
DKMS: build start for nvidia-560.45
make: Entering directory '/var/lib/dkms/nvidia/560.45/build'
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcuda
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[1]: *** [modules] Error 2
DKMS: build failed
```
maria: that -lcuda missing smells like CUDA toolkit was not staged on the image or rpath linker flags changed. we recently switched to the distro's cuda-toolkit packaging in the image.
kevin: confirmed: base image now has /usr/lib/cuda (distro-managed) instead of /usr/local/cuda. DKMS uses hardcoded /usr/local path during module link.
raj: possible quick fix: set CUDA_HOME to /usr/lib/cuda or symlink /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/lib/cuda in the initramfs build hook. any objections?
ashley: can we avoid rebuilding whole image? this is blocking capacity — provisioning queue spiked and autoscaler can't launch replacements.
infra-bot: provisioning-queue us-central-1: 12 pending GPU nodes, expected capacity shortfall: 6 GPUs.
sre-oncall: if it's just path mismatch, a post-provision hook that creates the symlink would be fastest to mitigate. but we should be careful with canary.
kevin: deployed a canary host update (post-provision symlink script) to one AZ — provisioning succeeded and DKMS now builds.
maria: long term we should update our DKMS packaging to pick up distro cuda path or vendor the necessary symlink in the image manifest. also check for RPATH flags in the kernel module build (we saw rpath entries earlier).
raj: also test with CUDA runtime 12.1 vs 12.0 — some symbols moved around and that could explain -lcuda link failures when mixed.
ashley: timeline: roll paused for full rollout, applying hotfix to canary cluster now. if hotfix works we can backfill pending nodes. expected catch-up time ~25m.
kevin: FYI this affects only the newer image variant that switched toolkit packaging; older image still provisions fine.
maria: note for postmortem — tag the image change with 'cuda-path-change' and include the DKMS build logs from the failing nodes.
ashley: agreed. Also putting a temporary capacity cushion on the autoscaler ( +10 GPUs ) to buy time for backfill to avoid customer throttles.
infra-bot: autoscaler-adjustment: +10 GPUs applied to us-central-1 for 30m.
sre-oncall: once canary is green, we should run a staggered resume and monitor NCCL job start failures (some reported later in thread earlier when driver loaded but userspace CUDA mismatched). keep eyes on job errors. :eyes:
raj: I'll follow up with a rebuild of the DKMS packaging to honor CUDA_HOME and add CI test for image/toolkit path permutations.
ashley: thanks — will update on rollback/finish. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary-hotfix deployed to 3 hosts (us-central-1a,1b), roll status: success on canary.
